map.summary: This document provides a comprehensive datasheet overview for the STM32F103xC/xD/xE high-density performance-line microcontrollers. It describes the Cortex-M3 architecture, memory and pin mappings, peripherals, clocks, interrupts, power management, and external-memory support, alongside electrical, thermal, timing, and current-consumption specifications. It also details oscillator and PLL behavior, Flash characteristics, FSMC and communication-interface timing, analog performance, package dimensions and PCB guidance, device markings, ordering codes, and datasheet revision information.
map.shortDescription: A comprehensive reference to STM32F103xC/xD/xE features, electrical and timing specifications, interfaces, packages, and ordering information.

sections.title: STM32F103xC/D/E high-density performance line
sections.summary: Datasheet production data for the STM32F103xC, STM32F103xD, and STM32F103xE high-density performance-line MCUs. The feature overview describes an Arm Cortex-M3 core running at up to 72 MHz; 256–512 KB of Flash and up to 64 KB of SRAM; FSMC and LCD parallel interface; timers and watchdogs; clock, reset, power, and low-power features; and communication interfaces including I²C, USART, SPI, I²S, CAN, USB, and SDIO. It also lists ADCs, DACs, DMA, CRC, debug facilities, fast I/O, supported packages, and device ordering groups.
sections.shortDescription: Introduces the STM32F103xC, xD, and xE microcontrollers and summarizes their core, memory, peripherals, package options, and key capabilities.

sections.title: Contents and datasheet organization
sections.summary: The contents pages outline the datasheet structure. They cover device description and overview; core, Flash, SRAM, CRC, FSMC, LCD interface, interrupts, clocks, boot modes, power, DMA, RTC, timers, and communication and analog peripherals. Later chapters address pinouts, memory mapping, electrical characteristics and operating conditions, clock and memory characteristics, I/O and interface specifications, ADC/DAC and temperature-sensor data, package information, ordering information, and revision history.
sections.shortDescription: Lists the datasheet chapters and subsections, from device architecture and pinouts to electrical characteristics, package information, and ordering.

sections.title: List of tables: device, operating, and electrical specifications
sections.summary: The table index identifies reference tables for device features and peripheral counts, family compatibility, timer comparisons, pin definitions, and FSMC signals. It then lists electrical and thermal operating limits, power-up/down and reset characteristics, internal reference voltage, current-consumption data across Run, Sleep, Stop, and Standby modes, and peripheral current. Additional entries cover external and internal oscillators, PLL, wake-up timing, Flash endurance and retention, and extensive FSMC read/write timings for SRAM, PSRAM, NOR, PC Card/CF, and NAND. The final entries in this window point to electromagnetic and electrical sensitivity, I/O injection and static/AC characteristics, NRST, and timer specifications.
sections.shortDescription: Catalogs datasheet tables covering device features, pin definitions, operating conditions, current use, clocks, memories, I/O, and interfaces.

sections.title: Tables and figures index; STM32F103xC/D/E introduction and device overview
sections.summary: Lines 276–309 complete the list of tables, covering I²C, SPI, I²S, SD/MMC, USB, ADC, DAC, temperature-sensor, package-mechanical, thermal, and ordering information. Lines 311–425 list figures, including block diagrams, clock tree, package pinouts, memory map, electrical and peripheral timing diagrams, ADC/DAC connections, and package outlines and footprints. From line 427, the datasheet introduces the STM32F103xC/D/E family: Arm Cortex-M3 devices operating at up to 72 MHz, with up to 512 KB Flash and 64 KB SRAM, broad I/O and peripheral options, a 2.0–3.6 V supply range, and a −40 to +105 °C operating range. The overview notes applications and six package types, and begins a device feature-count table comparing the STM32F103Rx, STM32F103Vx, and STM32F103Zx variants, including memory, FSMC, timers, communication interfaces, GPIOs, ADCs, DACs, and CPU frequency.
sections.shortDescription: Lists the datasheet’s electrical-characteristics tables and figures, then introduces the STM32F103xC/D/E high-density performance-line microcontrollers and summarizes their features and peripheral counts.

sections.title: Device specifications and block diagrams
sections.summary: Lists operating voltage, temperature ranges, package options and package-specific FSMC limitations. Presents the STM32F103xC/D/E performance-line block diagram and clock tree, with notes on system-clock limits, USB clock requirements and ADC conversion timing.
sections.shortDescription: Covers device operating conditions, package information, hardware diagrams, and clock configuration constraints.

sections.title: Family compatibility and overview
sections.summary: Explains how STM32F103xC/D/E devices relate to other density classes and summarizes the family’s memory and peripheral configurations. Describes the Cortex-M3 core, embedded Flash and SRAM, CRC calculation unit, and FSMC features and performance.
sections.shortDescription: Summarizes family compatibility and memory/peripheral differences, then introduces core features and the FSMC.

sections.title: LCD interface and interrupt controller
sections.summary: Covers the STM32F103’s system architecture and peripherals, including FSMC-based parallel LCD interfacing in Intel 8080 and Motorola 6800 modes; NVIC and external interrupt handling; clocks, boot options, power supervision, voltage regulation, and low-power modes; DMA, RTC, backup registers, timers, watchdogs, and SysTick; and communication interfaces such as I²C, USART/UART, SPI, I²S, SDIO, CAN, and USB.
sections.shortDescription: Surveys STM32F103 system features, interrupt and power management, timers, and communication peripherals, including FSMC support for parallel LCDs.

sections.title: Overview of the STM32F103xC/D/E peripherals and package pinout diagrams.
sections.summary: The STM32F103xC/D/E overview describes its USB full-speed peripheral, configurable GPIO, three 12-bit ADCs, dual 12-bit DACs, temperature sensor, SWJ-DP debugging, and ETM tracing. It also summarizes ADC and DAC features, shows package pinout diagrams, and details pin definitions and alternate-function mappings for PE2 through PB1 across several package variants.
sections.shortDescription: Overview of STM32F103xC/D/E peripherals, package pinouts, and pin functions from PE2 through PB1.

sections.title: High-density STM32F103xC/D/E pin definitions (continued)
sections.summary: Continues Table 5 with pin definitions beginning at PB2 and progressing through PF11–PF15, PG0–PG1, PE7–PE15, and PB10–PB13. It includes power pins between signal groups and gives package-specific positions, pin types, reset states, and alternate functions. Mappings include FSMC address and data signals, TIM1 and TIM2 functions, USART3, I2C2, SPI2, and I2S2. The passage also contains the continuation of a footnote marker for optional alternate-function availability.
sections.shortDescription: Continues pin assignments from PB2 through PB13, with package positions and FSMC, timer, USART, I2C, and SPI alternate functions.

sections.title: High-density STM32F103xC/D/E pin definitions (continued)
sections.summary: Continues the high-density device pin table. Covers PB14–PB15, PD8–PD15, PG2–PG8, and supply pins VSS_8, VDD_8, VSS_9, and VDD_9. The listed alternate functions include SPI2 and I2S2 signals, USART3, FSMC data and address lines, TIM4 channels, and TIM8/SDIO/I2S functions on PC6 and PC7, with timer remaps also indicated. Package coordinates and pin numbers are provided where applicable.
sections.shortDescription: Lists further pin mappings from PB14 and PB15 through PD8–PD15, PG2–PG8, and PC6–PC7.

sections.title: High-density STM32F103xC/D/E pin definitions and notes
sections.summary: Continues the high-density device pin-definition table, covering PC8–PC9 and PA8–PA15, PC10–PC12, PD0–PD7, PG9–PG15, PB3–PB9, BOOT0, and PE0–PE1. Rows give package pin numbers, I/O types and levels, reset defaults, and alternate functions such as timers, USART/UART, SDIO, FSMC, CAN, SPI, I2C, and debug signals. The accompanying notes explain 5 V tolerance and supply/input/output abbreviations, peripheral clock conflicts, output limitations for PC13–PC15, backup-domain behavior, WLCSP/64-pin package exceptions, remapping, and FSMC unavailability in LQFP64.
sections.shortDescription: Pin assignments, alternate functions, and explanatory notes for high-density STM32F103xC/D/E packages.

sections.title: FSMC pin definition table
sections.summary: Introduces Table 6, mapping FSMC pins to functions for LQFP100 and BGA100 configurations and for CF, CF/IDE, NOR/PSRAM/SRAM, and 16-bit NAND interfaces. The entries cover PE2–PE6 address lines; PF0–PF5 address lines; PF6–PF11 CompactFlash control/status signals; PF12–PF15 and PG0–PG1 address lines; PE7–PE15 data lines; PD8–PD10 data lines; and PD11–PD12 address/control signals. The continuation identifies whether each pin is available in BGA100 and lists NAND-specific signals such as DA lines, CLE, and ALE.
sections.shortDescription: Maps FSMC signals to pins for supported memory and interface configurations.

sections.title: FSMC Pin Alternate Functions
sections.summary: The pin-function table covers PD13–PD15, PG2–PG7, PD0–PD1, PD3–PD7, PG9–PG14, PB7, and PE0–PE1. Entries identify address and data lines, clock and read/write controls, chip enables, wait, address-valid, and byte-lane signals. A final column marks applicable pin availability or related status.
sections.shortDescription: Lists device pins and their alternate-function signals for FSMC memory interfaces, including NOR/PSRAM, NAND, and related control signals.

sections.title: Memory Map
sections.summary: The memory map identifies FSMC registers and external-memory banks: NOR/PSRAM bank 1, NAND banks 2 and 3, and PCCARD bank 4. It also lays out the peripheral address space, including CRC, flash interface, RCC, SDIO, USARTs, SPI, timers, FSMC registers, CAN, USB/CAN SRAM, and watchdogs. Larger regions are divided into 512-Mbyte blocks, with Cortex-M3 peripherals in the system region. The map shows code and reserved regions, 64-Kbyte SRAM, flash, system-memory and boot aliases, and the flash and SRAM bit-band alias ranges. The following electrical-characteristics material introduces parameter conditions and typical values, pin loading and input-voltage figures, and the power-supply and current-measurement schemes.
sections.shortDescription: Presents the STM32F103xC/xD/xE memory map, showing FSMC banks, peripheral address regions, SRAM, flash, reserved space, and boot aliases.

sections.title: Electrical Characteristics and Absolute Maximum Ratings
sections.summary: The electrical-characteristics section shows the power-supply scheme, including backup circuitry, digital and analog supplies, regulator decoupling, and ADC reference connections; it cautions that the 4.7 pF capacitor belongs on VDD3. A current-consumption measurement diagram follows. The absolute-maximum-ratings introduction warns that exceeding listed limits can permanently damage the device and that these are stress ratings, not functional operating conditions. Voltage ratings cover main supply voltage, input limits for five-volt-tolerant and other pins, variations among supply and ground pins, and electrostatic discharge. Notes require all main supply and ground pins to be connected within the permitted range, require respecting VIN and injected-current limits, and include VREF− in the ground-variation consideration. Current ratings list total supply and ground currents, per-pin output currents, injected-current limits, and the total injected-current limit across I/O and control pins.
sections.shortDescription: Introduces the supply and current-consumption measurement diagrams, then gives voltage and current absolute maximum ratings with key notes.

sections.title: Operating conditions and power-up characteristics
sections.summary: This section gives electrical safety notes for power and ground pins and injection currents, followed by thermal ratings and general operating limits. It specifies clock, voltage, power-dissipation, and temperature ranges, power-up/down supply slew requirements, programmable voltage detector thresholds, power-on/power-down reset thresholds and reset timing, and internal reference voltage characteristics.
sections.shortDescription: Covers thermal and operating limits, supply sequencing, reset and voltage-detector thresholds, and the embedded reference voltage.

sections.title: Run-mode and Sleep-mode current consumption
sections.summary: This section describes current-consumption measurement conditions and presents maximum Run-mode current for code executing from Flash or RAM, with external-clock peripherals enabled or disabled across HCLK frequencies and two ambient temperatures. It also includes typical Run-mode consumption plots and maximum Sleep-mode current under corresponding clock and peripheral conditions, with characterization and clock-source notes.
sections.shortDescription: Presents current-consumption test conditions, Run-mode tables and plots, and maximum Sleep-mode current across clock frequencies.

sections.title: Stop- and Standby-mode current-consumption table
sections.summary: Introduces Table 17, which reports typical and maximum current consumption in Stop and Standby modes across supply-voltage and ambient-temperature conditions. The assigned lines include the table heading and its column headers.
sections.shortDescription: Begins the table of typical and maximum Stop- and Standby-mode current consumption.

sections.title: MCU Supply Current and Run-Mode Consumption
sections.summary: This section presents supply-current data for Stop, Standby, and backup-domain operation, along with temperature-related current-consumption plots. It then gives typical Run-mode current for code executing from Flash at a range of HCLK frequencies, comparing all peripherals enabled with all peripherals disabled, and distinguishing external-clock from HSI operation. Measurement conditions and notes on typical values are included.
sections.shortDescription: Covers supply current in low-power states and typical current consumption in Run mode across clock frequencies and peripheral activity.

sections.title: Sleep-Mode Current Consumption
sections.summary: The table lists typical current consumption in Sleep mode for code running from Flash or RAM. Values are provided across HCLK frequencies with all peripherals enabled or disabled, for external-clock and HSI configurations. Notes specify the measurement conditions and explain additional ADC analog-current consumption when the ADC is enabled.
sections.shortDescription: Reports typical Sleep-mode current across clock frequencies, peripheral states, and clock-source configurations.

sections.title: On-Chip Peripheral Current Consumption
sections.summary: The section defines how peripheral current is measured, then tabulates consumption per MHz for AHB, APB1, and APB2 peripherals. Listed blocks include DMA, FSMC, CRC, SDIO, timers, serial interfaces, GPIO ports, ADCs, DAC, USB, CAN, and watchdogs. Footnotes describe BusMatrix activation, added current for I2S and DAC operation, and the conditions and analog-current increment associated with enabled ADCs.
sections.shortDescription: Lists clocked peripheral current consumption by bus and provides measurement conditions and supplementary current notes.

sections.title: External Clock Source Characteristics
sections.summary: The tables specify electrical characteristics for externally generated high-speed and low-speed clocks, including frequency ranges, input voltage levels, timing and rise/fall limits, input capacitance, duty cycle, and leakage current. The LSE duty cycle is 30–70%, and OSC32_IN leakage is limited to ±1 µA for input voltages between VSS and VDD. Specifications are guaranteed by design under the stated ambient-temperature and supply-voltage conditions.
sections.shortDescription: Covers electrical limits for external high-speed and low-speed clock inputs, including LSE duty cycle and OSC32_IN leakage.

sections.title: External clock timing diagrams
sections.summary: This section presents the high-speed external clock source timing diagram and the low-speed external clock source timing diagram, identifying clock edges, timing intervals, and oscillator input/output signals.
sections.shortDescription: Shows AC timing diagrams for high-speed and low-speed external clock sources.

sections.title: High-speed external crystal oscillator
sections.summary: The HSE oscillator supports 4–16 MHz crystals or ceramic resonators. The table specifies frequency, feedback resistance, recommended load capacitance, driving current, transconductance, and startup time. The accompanying guidance covers component placement, crystal-dependent characteristics, load-capacitor selection, humidity considerations, startup-time variation, and the 8 MHz application circuit.
sections.shortDescription: Gives HSE crystal oscillator characteristics, design guidance, and a typical 8 MHz application circuit.

sections.title: Low-speed external crystal oscillator
sections.summary: The LSE oscillator uses a 32.768 kHz crystal or ceramic resonator. Its characteristics table gives feedback resistance, load capacitance, drive current, transconductance, and startup times across temperatures. Notes explain that startup depends on the crystal, PCB layout, and humidity. Capacitor sizing guidance gives the load-capacitance formula and typical stray capacitance; a caution recommends a resonator with CL ≤ 7 pF and warns against a 12.5 pF load. A typical crystal application is illustrated.
sections.shortDescription: Describes LSE oscillator characteristics and capacitor selection for a 32.768 kHz crystal circuit.

sections.title: High-speed internal RC oscillator
sections.summary: The HSI RC oscillator characteristics include an 8 MHz frequency, a 45–55% duty cycle after user trimming, accuracy limits under specified temperatures, startup-time figures, and 80–100 µA power consumption. Notes identify the supply and temperature conditions, point to the HSI calibration application note, and state which specifications are guaranteed by design or characterization.
sections.shortDescription: Lists HSI oscillator frequency, duty cycle, accuracy, startup time, power, and related conditions.

sections.title: Low-speed internal RC oscillator
sections.summary: The LSI RC oscillator is specified at 30–60 kHz, with a typical startup time of 85 µs and power consumption of 0.65–1.2 µA. The stated test conditions are VDD = 3 V and TA = −40 to 105 °C; guarantees are by characterization or design.
sections.shortDescription: Provides LSI oscillator frequency, startup time, power consumption, and test conditions.

sections.title: Low-power mode wakeup timings
sections.summary: Wakeup timing measurements use an 8 MHz HSI RC oscillator. Stop and Standby wakeups use the RC oscillator, while Sleep resumes with the clock configured before entry. Typical wakeup times are 1.8 µs from Sleep, 3.6 or 5.4 µs from Stop depending on regulator mode, and 50 µs from Standby. Timing runs from the wakeup event until application code reads its first instruction.
sections.shortDescription: Explains wakeup clock sources and gives typical wakeup times from Sleep, Stop, and Standby modes.

sections.title: PLL and Flash memory characteristics
sections.summary: PLL specifications include an 18–25 MHz input clock, 40–60% input duty cycle, 16–72 MHz multiplier output, a maximum 200 µs lock time, and 300 ps cycle-to-cycle jitter. The Flash table gives programming and erase times, supply-current figures for operating modes, and a 2–3.6 V programming-voltage range. Notes specify temperature conditions, the need to keep PLL input values within range, and a design guarantee.
sections.shortDescription: Specifies PLL clock and lock characteristics alongside Flash programming, erase, current, and voltage limits.

sections.title: Flash endurance and data retention table heading
sections.summary: The section ends by opening Table 30, which covers Flash memory endurance and data retention; the table’s data continues beyond the assigned lines.
sections.shortDescription: Introduces the Flash memory endurance and data retention specifications.

sections.title: Summarizes memory endurance and retention specifications and FSMC asynchronous and synchronous interface timing conditions.
sections.summary: The section reports STM32F103xC/xD/xE nonvolatile-memory endurance and data-retention figures, then details FSMC asynchronous and synchronous interface timing. Asynchronous specifications cover non-multiplexed SRAM/PSRAM/NOR and multiplexed PSRAM/NOR reads and writes, including stated configuration parameters and a 15 pF load for characterized results. Synchronous timing tables cover multiplexed PSRAM and non-multiplexed NOR/PSRAM read and write operations, including clock, chip-enable, address, control-signal, data-valid, and NWAIT timing, with associated waveform diagrams.
sections.shortDescription: Covers memory endurance and retention figures and FSMC asynchronous and synchronous read/write timing specifications, conditions, and waveforms.

sections.title: PC Card and CompactFlash Controller Waveforms
sections.summary: This section introduces PC Card/CompactFlash controller waveforms and timings. Figures 32–37 are identified as synchronous waveforms, with corresponding timings in Table 39. The stated FSMC configuration sets setup, wait, hold, and HiZ times for common memory, attribute memory, and I/O, and sets TCLR and TAR setup times to zero. The included figures depict common-memory read and write accesses and attribute-memory read access. A note specifies that FSMC_NCE4_2 remains high (inactive) during an 8-bit access.
sections.shortDescription: Introduces synchronous PC Card/CompactFlash waveform timing and shows common-memory read/write and attribute-memory read access diagrams.

sections.title: PC Card/CompactFlash controller timing
sections.summary: Shows PC Card/CompactFlash controller waveforms for attribute-memory writes and I/O-space reads and writes, then gives switching timing limits for PC Card/CF read and write cycles. The timing table covers address and control-signal validity, read/write pulse widths, data setup and hold behavior, and NIOWR/NIORD timing. Test notes specify a 15 pF load and that some values are guaranteed by characterization.
sections.shortDescription: Figures and switching characteristics for PC Card/CompactFlash attribute memory and I/O-space accesses, including read and write timing parameters.

sections.title: NAND controller waveforms and timing
sections.summary: Introduces the FSMC configuration used for the NAND controller timing results, including setup, wait, hold, and HiZ values for common and attribute banks, 16-bit data width, ECC settings, and zero TAR/TCLR setup times. Figures show NAND read and write accesses and common-memory read and write accesses. The switching-characteristics table specifies data-valid timing, NWE pulse widths, ALE timing, and related read/write constraints. Notes identify the capacitive load and whether results are guaranteed by characterization or design.
sections.shortDescription: NAND Flash controller read/write waveforms and switching characteristics for NAND and common-memory accesses.

sections.title: EMC, ESD, latch-up, and current-injection susceptibility
sections.summary: Describes fast-transient immunity and software practices for managing EMC-related faults, including runaway execution, unexpected resets, and critical data corruption. It gives EMI emissions results and SAE EMI level, then lists ESD ratings for human-body and charged-device models and explains the latch-up tests. The I/O injection discussion outlines test conditions, functional-failure criteria, and the stated negative and positive current limits for groups of pins.
sections.shortDescription: This section covers EMC test results, ESD and latch-up ratings, and the device’s functional susceptibility to injected I/O current.

sections.title: I/O static input characteristics
sections.summary: Introduces general I/O characteristics and tabulates input low and high voltage thresholds for standard and five-volt-tolerant pins, Schmitt-trigger hysteresis, input leakage, weak pull-up and pull-down resistance, and pin capacitance. Notes that the I/Os are CMOS- and TTL-compliant, explains the FT designation, and describes the series resistance and switchable PMOS/NMOS structure of pull resistors. The accompanying figures illustrate standard and 5 V-tolerant input ranges for CMOS and TTL levels.
sections.shortDescription: This section gives static electrical limits and typical characteristics for MCU input and bidirectional I/O pins.

sections.title: I/O input-level characteristic figures
sections.summary: Contains the graphical input-characteristic material referenced by the static I/O specifications. The figures compare standard-port CMOS and TTL requirements with five-volt-tolerant input characteristics, showing threshold regions and ranges that are not guaranteed. The diagrams complement the numerical voltage limits and clarify how input levels relate to the supply voltage.
sections.shortDescription: This section presents diagrams of input voltage ranges for standard and five-volt-tolerant I/O ports.

sections.title: GPIO output drive and voltage characteristics
sections.summary: Continues the input-characteristic diagrams, then describes GPIO output-current capability: general pins can source or sink up to ±8 mA, with higher current possible under relaxed output-voltage limits, while PC13–PC15 are limited to ±3 mA and 2 MHz under the stated load. It warns that total sourced and sunk currents must remain within absolute maximum ratings. The output-voltage table specifies low- and high-level limits when eight pins operate simultaneously, including TTL- and CMOS-port conditions.
sections.shortDescription: This section explains GPIO current-drive restrictions and provides output voltage limits for standard I/O loading conditions.

sections.title: Output voltage limits and notes
sections.summary: Completes the GPIO output-voltage specifications for eight simultaneously driven pins, including limits at 20 mA and 6 mA and the corresponding supply-voltage ranges. Notes that per-pin and summed I/O currents must comply with the device absolute maximum ratings and supply-current limits, and states compatibility with JEDEC TTL and CMOS output standards. Characterization-based guarantees are identified.
sections.shortDescription: This section continues the output-voltage table with higher-current and supply-dependent GPIO limits and associated cautions.

sections.title: I/O AC characteristics
sections.summary: Presents GPIO AC characteristics, including output frequency limits, rise and fall times, and EXTI pulse-width limits for different output-speed settings and specified loads and supply ranges. It also explains GPIO speed configuration and details NRST electrical characteristics, including its CMOS input, permanent pull-up, low-level voltage and Schmitt-trigger hysteresis, plus recommended protection against parasitic resets.
sections.shortDescription: Covers GPIO timing and speed characteristics alongside NRST electrical specifications and reset-pin protection guidance.

sections.title: TIM timer characteristics
sections.summary: Introduces TIM timer characteristics, which are guaranteed by design, and refers readers to the GPIO characteristics for alternate-function I/O details. Table 50 gives a 13.9 ns timer resolution at a 72 MHz timer clock, a maximum external clock frequency of 36 MHz, and 16-bit counter timing limits: a 0.0139 µs minimum period and a 910 µs maximum period when using the internal clock. The maximum possible count is 59.6 seconds. TIMx denotes TIM1 through TIM4.
sections.shortDescription: Presents timer resolution, external clock frequency, counter period, and maximum count specifications.

sections.title: I2C interface characteristics
sections.summary: Documents I2C protocol characteristics and timing limits for standard and fast modes, including clock low/high periods, data setup and hold times, rise and fall times, start/stop timing, bus-free time, bus capacitance, and analog-filter spike suppression. It notes that SDA and SCL are not true open-drain outputs because a PMOS remains physically present when disabled. The section includes the AC waveform and measurement circuit, explains the timing points and external resistors, and provides example SCL frequencies and CCR settings for a 36 MHz PCLK1 and 3.3 V bus supply. It also specifies clock-source frequency requirements and expected frequency tolerances.
sections.shortDescription: Describes I2C electrical timing, bus waveforms, clock settings, and the conditions and notes for standard and fast modes.

sections.title: SPI electrical characteristics
sections.summary: Introduces SPI and I2S interface measurement conditions, then presents SPI limits including clock frequency, clock transitions, slave input duty cycle, NSS setup and hold times, SCK high/low timing, data input setup and hold, and data output access, disable, valid, and hold times. Notes clarify characterization guarantees and output timing interpretations. The section then begins SPI slave timing diagrams for CPHA = 0 and CPHA = 1.
sections.shortDescription: Lists SPI electrical and timing specifications and begins the slave-mode timing diagrams.

sections.title: SPI and I2S timing characteristics
sections.summary: The section finishes SPI timing information, then gives I2S clock-frequency and duty-cycle limits, clock rise/fall times, and WS and serial-data setup, hold, and valid-time specifications for master and slave modes. It also references Philips-protocol I2S slave and master timing diagrams and notes measurement levels and characterization qualifications.
sections.shortDescription: This section presents SPI master timing and I2S electrical and timing characteristics, including clock, WS, and serial-data timing parameters and timing diagrams.

sections.title: SDIO and SD/MMC interface characteristics
sections.summary: The SDIO/SD/MMC characteristics are specified under the stated ambient, clock, and supply conditions, with I/O details referenced elsewhere. The tables cover transfer-mode clock frequency, clock high and low times, rise and fall times, CMD and data input setup and hold times, and output valid and hold times for high-speed and default modes. The clock output is controlled through the SDIO clock control register.
sections.shortDescription: This section describes SDIO clock and signal timing requirements for SD/MMC cards, including high-speed and default modes.

sections.title: USB electrical characteristics
sections.summary: The USB interface is identified as USB-IF certified for full speed. Specifications include a 1 µs transceiver startup time, operating voltage and receiver thresholds, and static output levels. Notes describe the D+ pull-up requirement, operation at reduced supply voltage, and measurement conditions. Full-speed driver characteristics define data rise and fall times, their matching, and crossover voltage, with measurement intervals and USB specification references provided.
sections.shortDescription: This section covers USB full-speed startup, DC voltage levels, and data-signal timing characteristics.

sections.title: 12-bit ADC characteristics and input impedance
sections.summary: This section covers ADC operating limits and conversion timing, including reference and supply ranges, clock and sampling rates, calibration and power-up times, and trigger latency. It provides the formula and lookup table for maximum source impedance at a 14 MHz ADC clock, then describes accuracy test conditions and error limits for two device groups. It defines total unadjusted, offset, gain, differential-linearity, and integral-linearity errors, warns about negative injection current, and gives ADC connection and reference-decoupling guidance, including package limitations for VREF pins.
sections.shortDescription: ADC operating and timing specifications, source-impedance limits, accuracy characteristics, and connection and reference-decoupling guidance.

sections.title: DAC electrical specifications
sections.summary: Lists DAC operating supplies and reference requirements, output limits with the buffer enabled or disabled, quiescent current under several codes, and specified integral and differential nonlinearity. Provides load and output-impedance limits, offset and gain error, settling and wakeup times, maximum update rate, and PSRR. Clarifies that the DAC output buffer can lower output impedance and drive external loads, and can be bypassed through the DAC control register.
sections.shortDescription: DAC supply, output-range, current, linearity, load, settling-time, update-rate, wakeup, and power-supply rejection specifications.

sections.title: Temperature sensor characteristics
sections.summary: Specifies temperature-sensor linearity over temperature, average voltage slope, and sensor voltage at 25 °C. Gives startup time and ADC sampling-time information, with a note that applications can determine the shortest sampling time by repeated measurements. Startup-time data is guaranteed by design.
sections.shortDescription: Temperature-sensor voltage, linearity, average slope, and startup and ADC sampling-time specifications.

sections.title: LFBGA144 package information and mechanical data
sections.summary: Introduces ST’s ECOPACK environmental-compliance information and presents the LFBGA144 package outline for a 144-ball, 10 × 10 mm low-profile fine-pitch ball grid array with 0.8 mm pitch. It covers package mechanical dimensions in metric and imperial units and recommended PCB footprint rules, including pad, UBM, solder-mask, stencil, and trace dimensions. The package drawing is not to scale.
sections.shortDescription: Covers ECOPACK information, LFBGA144 package dimensions, and recommended PCB footprint rules for its 0.8 mm pitch.

sections.title: LFBGA144 and LFBGA100 Marking and Package Information
sections.summary: Explains the LFBGA144 marking orientation and A1 ball identifier, with an engineering-sample qualification notice. Introduces the LFBGA100 package, shows its outline and mechanical dimensions, provides recommended PCB design rules for the 0.8 mm pitch package, and presents its marking example and related notice.
sections.shortDescription: Covers LFBGA144 and LFBGA100 package marking examples and the LFBGA100 outline, mechanical dimensions, and PCB design guidance.

sections.title: WLCSP64 Package Dimensions and PCB Design Rules
sections.summary: Describes the 64-ball WLCSP outline and its datums, then tabulates package dimensions in millimeters and inches, including ball size, pitch, package dimensions, and ball count. Provides recommended footprint and PCB design values, with continuation details for stencil thickness, pad trace width, and ball diameter.
sections.shortDescription: Presents the WLCSP64 package outline, mechanical dimensions, and recommended PCB design rules for a 0.5 mm pitch.

sections.title: LQFP144 Package Outline and Mechanical Data
sections.summary: Begins the LQFP144 package-information section with the 144-pin, 20 × 20 mm low-profile quad flat package outline. Notes that the drawing is not to scale and introduces the mechanical-data table, which reports dimensions in millimeters and inches; the table continues beyond this excerpt.
sections.shortDescription: Introduces the LQFP144 package outline and begins its mechanical-data table.

sections.title: LQFP144 package footprint and marking
sections.summary: Provides the LQFP144 package mechanical-data dimensions in millimeters and inches, followed by the recommended PCB footprint and its units. It also shows the package-top marking example, including pin 1 identification and device-code orientation, and includes the engineering-sample qualification disclaimer.
sections.shortDescription: This section covers LQFP144 mechanical dimensions, recommended footprint, and device marking guidance.

sections.title: LQFP100 package information
sections.summary: Documents the LQFP100 14 × 14 mm, 100-pin package outline and mechanical dimensions, including the continuation of the dimension table and inch-conversion note. It also presents the recommended footprint and a package-top marking example with revision, date, and pin 1 indicators, followed by the engineering-sample disclaimer.
sections.shortDescription: This section covers the LQFP100 outline, dimensional data, PCB footprint, and top-side device marking.

sections.title: LQFP64 package information
sections.summary: Presents the LQFP64 10 × 10 mm package outline and mechanical-data tables in millimeters and inches, including the continued dimensions and conversion note. It includes the recommended PCB footprint and an example of top-side marking orientation and pin 1 identification, together with the engineering-sample qualification disclaimer.
sections.shortDescription: This section describes LQFP64 package dimensions, footprint guidance, and device marking orientation.

sections.title: Thermal characteristics and product temperature range
sections.summary: Explains the maximum junction-temperature limit and estimates junction temperature from ambient temperature, package junction-to-ambient thermal resistance, and total power dissipation. It defines internal and I/O power contributions, lists thermal resistance values for supported packages, cites the JESD51-2 reference, and begins guidance for choosing the product temperature-range suffix based on application dissipation and junction temperature.
sections.shortDescription: This section explains junction-temperature estimation, package thermal resistance, and how to select a temperature range.

sections.title: Product temperature examples and ordering scheme
sections.summary: Two worked calculations show how power dissipation and junction temperature determine the required temperature-range suffix: a high-performance case requiring suffix 6 and a high-ambient, lower-dissipation case requiring suffix 7. The section also explains the ordering-code fields for device family, type, subfamily, pin count, Flash size, package, temperature range, and options.
sections.shortDescription: Worked temperature-range calculations and an explanation of the STM32F103 ordering code.

sections.title: Revision history
sections.summary: The revision history tracks datasheet updates from the initial release through revision 13, including changes to device features and pin definitions, electrical and timing specifications, figures and tables, ADC and DAC specifications, peripheral counts, package and mechanical data, ordering information, and the addition of the WLCSP64 package. The section concludes with STMicroelectronics’ notice on changing product information, purchaser responsibilities, sales terms, intellectual property, trademarks, and superseded document versions.
sections.shortDescription: Chronological summary of STM32F103 datasheet revisions and package updates, followed by STMicroelectronics’ important notice and legal terms.
